coverage_gaps: The merged candidate universe remains U.S. electrical-infrastructure heavy because the visible Layer 1B candidate evidence was concentrated in switchgear, transformers, electrical installation, and grid-interconnection hardware.

Need broader non-U.S. candidate discovery across Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Europe, Canada, and Australia, especially for transformer components, power semiconductors, memory substrates, advanced packaging materials, test equipment, thermal materials, and critical-mineral processing.
Need current market-cap, liquidity, analyst-coverage, and revenue-purity checks for each ticker; several provided market-cap buckets appear stale or approximate and should be validated in Layer 2.
Need primary filing checks for each underfollowed candidate: backlog, revenue by segment, customer concentration, capex, capacity expansion, margin expansion, and cancellation language.
Need regional grid mapping by PJM, ERCOT, MISO, SPP, and WECC to identify whether specific equipment or service providers have exposure to the most constrained data-center load pockets.

Need transformer and switchgear lead-time verification by supplier type: dry-type transformers, large power transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, busway, control buildings, substation connectors, and electrical steel laminations.

Need memory/HBM second-order universe expansion beyond obvious memory majors into test, substrates, packaging materials, thermal interface materials, probe cards, specialty gases, and refurbished enterprise storage channels.
Need critical-mineral universe expansion beyond reference rare-earth names into antimony, tungsten, graphite, gallium, germanium, and heavy rare-earth processors with listed-company mappings.

Need falsification checks for AI capex digestion risk: hyperscaler capex cuts, data-center project delays, interconnection cancellations, memory price normalization, power-project cancellations, regulatory pushback against data-center load growth, or transformer/switchgear capacity additions catching up faster than expected.

memory_update.text: The New Hotspots funnel should emphasize demand shocks migrating from obvious AI compute into physical-infrastructure chokepoints: electrical equipment, grid interconnection, generation, storage, memory supply, and critical minerals.

Switchgear, transformers, control buildings, bus systems, electrical installation capacity, substation connectors, and transformer-core materials are the highest-confidence underfollowed nodes in the current Layer 1 universe.

Powell, IES Holdings, Hammond Power Solutions, Preformed Line Products, and Worthington Steel represent the clearest current underfollowed or second-order mappings to the AI/data-center electrical bottleneck, subject to Layer 2 filing validation.
Reference leaders such as Eaton and GE Vernova should be used as demand validators and market-pricing checks, not allowed to crowd out smaller suppliers in the main alpha-discovery lane.

Layer 1C remains too narrow outside U.S. electrical infrastructure; the next run should expand global candidates in memory/HBM second-order suppliers, power semiconductors, battery storage, nuclear fuel, and critical-mineral processing.

Layer 2 must verify market cap, analyst coverage, revenue purity, backlog quality, customer concentration, margin conversion, and liquidity before any candidate survives into a high-conviction research list.

summary: Layer 1C merged universe for New Hotspots. The strongest current cluster is AI/data-center physical infrastructure, especially switchgear, transformers, electrical installation, grid interconnection hardware, and behind-the-meter/on-site power. The universe intentionally keeps reference leaders as demand validators while prioritizing underfollowed or second-order public names where bottleneck exposure is more hidden. Because the provided Layer 1B evidence is U.S. electrical-infrastructure heavy, candidates outside this node are included only selectively as hypotheses or reference anchors, and broader global coverage remains a key gap.
